newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Jochen Kubosch briefed on Friday's Telecommunications Council. Ministers should reach a common position on a proposed directive on authorising telecommunications operators and licences and on satellite personal communication services. But he added that agreement on liberalisation of postal services would be more difficult. Kubosch also said there might be ad hoc discussions on illegal messages in telecommunication services and on future initiatives in this field.

In answer to a question, spokeswoman Heike Gerstbrein denied Spanish press reports that the Commission had suspended cohesion funds to Spain for one month until it published its 1997 budget. Gerstbrein said the Commission was still looking at the numbers and that no agreement had yet been reached between the Commission and the Spanish government.

Asked about the Commission's reaction to recent violence in the Palestinian territories, spokesman Josep Coll i Carbo said the Irish Presidency was consulting its partners in the framework of the Common Foreign Security Policy to obtain a common position, possibly on Thursday.

Asked about the arrest of the mayor of Sint-Niklaas, Belgium, for fraud with money received from Commission's DGXXIII, spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said contacts had been made between Belgian authorities and the Commission unit responsible for the fight against fraud before the mayor's arrest and that an internal investigation had been launched.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/857: Commission publishes first balance sheet of fourth RDT framework programme.
- IP/96/858: Social security for migrant workers: a step towards the information society.
- IP/96/859: The task force on energy interconnections in the Balkans starts its activities.
- Speech/96/223: Speech by Commissionner Padraig Flynn on "the next steps on the EU's social and employment policy agenda".
- Press kit on trafficking in human beings for sexual purposes - Informal JHA Council.
- Eurobarometre: Poll of high level decision makers synthesis report.
- Eurostat, economy and finance, No 1996-8: taxes and social contributions in the European Union.
- Eurostat news release No 61/96: taxes and social contributions in the EU: 41.7% of GDP in 1995.
